about: Proposed verdicts for the 9-10 November 2026 direction (Frappe-native, one door). A proposal for the owner to correct by exception. Verdicts: core, plug, reached, dropped, aaron (operations and concepts); keep, rewrite, archive, aaron (decisions). A concept's `operationsStay` counts core and plug operations. Tables, machines, rpcs, flows, workflows, procedures, events and evals are counted by the verdict of the record that owns or drives them; the rule is in cut-proposal.md.

concepts.title: Access
concepts.reason: Sign-in, sessions and the machine's saved context. Identity is Core's; sign-in also becomes the Capxul provider that Frappe signs in through (a plug).

concepts.title: Media
concepts.reason: Stores the files Core itself needs (identity and bank verification documents). Frappe keeps its own files.

concepts.title: Parties
concepts.reason: The directory that maps a person or company to a Safe address. Core identity; Frappe's customer, supplier and contact records point at it.

concepts.title: Indexing
concepts.reason: The chain indexer's tables. Every Core fact and every chain event for the books come from here.

concepts.title: Approvals
concepts.reason: Every transaction a person signs. This is the signer that the held Frappe payment waits for.

concepts.title: Accounts
concepts.reason: A person's own account and Safe, and admission. Referrals and the waitlist stay for now (low confidence).

concepts.title: Organizations
concepts.reason: The organisation, its members, invitations, seats and setup. Reshape: setup now also creates the Frappe site. The Frappe 'head' tables and commands go or move to the plugs; the hosted FDE goes to Aaron.

concepts.title: Board
concepts.reason: Directors, proposals, officer hats and the Safe's approval threshold. Governance is kept (GROUNDING and START-HERE).

concepts.title: Agents
concepts.reason: Agents and their keys. They must wear hats like people (reshape: agent creation grants hats).

concepts.title: Projects
concepts.reason: Frappe owns projects and timesheets. Capxul's 10 tables, 3 machines and 35 operations go; the work is reached through the door.

concepts.title: Budgets
concepts.reason: Departments, budgets, ceilings and allowances: money authority on chain. Reshape: budgets as envelopes that follow Frappe's cost-centre tree, with the same periods.

concepts.title: Books
concepts.reason: Frappe owns the books. What stays is the chain reader that writes them (a plug): the feed of money facts, the asset list and the reversal rule.

concepts.title: Documents
concepts.reason: The hash of a document that a payment pays. Rendering and printing go to Frappe's print formats; the stamp and its verification stay.

concepts.title: Contacts
concepts.reason: Frappe owns the CRM and the address book. Capxul's 15 tables, 8 machines and 32 operations go. A wallet-address field on Frappe's parties (a plug) keeps payees payable.

concepts.title: Payments
concepts.reason: Payments in and out, scheduled and escrow, each paid under a hat and a budget. Reshape: every payment carries the document hash, the cost centre and the account code.

concepts.title: Payroll
concepts.reason: Frappe HR owns payroll, HR, leave, attendance and expense claims (76 of 87 operations). The 11 on-chain pay-agreement operations stay as Core (recommend moving them into payments). Paying a run goes through Core's payment.

replaces.module: Payroll; HR (Leaves, Attendance, Expense Claims, Shifts)

concepts.title: Banking
concepts.reason: Bridge bank details, deposits, payouts and identity checks. Banking is the revenue line (GROUNDING). Opening accounts and verification stay but are off the critical path.

concepts.title: Requests
concepts.reason: A payment request that any payer sees in an inbox, even without a Frappe site. Reshape: a Frappe Sales Invoice can issue one and carries its hash. Services (checkout items) go to Frappe.

concepts.title: Applications
concepts.reason: Publishable keys for people who build on the CLI and SDK. The door's purpose is that anyone can build on it.

concepts.title: Equity
concepts.reason: aaron.frappe-native keeps equity; START-HERE and GROUNDING drop it. Aaron settles it. No verdict until then.

concepts.title: Activity
concepts.reason: The read model of a person's or organisation's money: balance, address, payments feed. The notes and account stamps now travel on the payment.

concepts.title: Notices
concepts.reason: Emails after Core changes (money waiting, invitations, payments, board). The HR, payslip and head notices go (Frappe's own notifications do HR).

concepts.title: Devnet
concepts.reason: The local world: time, seasons, snapshots, mail, fake services. Needed to hill-climb. Reshape: the world must include a real Frappe site on the same clock.

newRecordsNeeded.title: Sites: a company's hosted Frappe site, its feature switches and the document door
newRecordsNeeded.why: Nothing in the book owns the site today; organizations holds a 'head' that is an outside site. One owner keeps the six-slot module small.

newRecordsNeeded.title: Plugs: sign-in, signer, roles that follow hats, books from the chain
newRecordsNeeded.why: These four joins cross concepts. They need one home in the dependency order, above payments and below sites.

newRecordsNeeded.title: The control plane that creates and runs sites
newRecordsNeeded.why: Frappe's open-source Press, or a thin script, creates a site in about two minutes (skeleton: 143 s). Today no component does it.

newRecordsNeeded.title: component:frappe-app is written for a connected head; rewrite it as the hosted app
newRecordsNeeded.why: Its text says it is the head's half of the frappe-head integration. The skeleton built it with no fork.

newRecordsNeeded.title: Capxul is the sign-in: an OAuth and OpenID provider that each site's Social Login Key points at
newRecordsNeeded.why: Frappe never holds keys or signs. Sign-up is denied: only a person a hat created can sign in. The skeleton did this with a stand-in provider.

newRecordsNeeded.title: One OAuth client per site: id, secret, exact redirect addresses
newRecordsNeeded.why: The stand-in accepted any redirect address; the real provider must match exactly (FINDINGS, Core half).

newRecordsNeeded.title: Authorize, token and userinfo (three rpcs)
newRecordsNeeded.why: They are the provider. Userinfo must be membership-aware: a person who is not in the organisation is refused.

newRecordsNeeded.title: A normal Frappe payment is held until the chain confirms
newRecordsNeeded.why: Frappe must never mark money moved before the chain says so. Skeleton: the form's Submit calls Capxul; a before-submit hook and a ledger hook refuse any other route; no fork.

newRecordsNeeded.title: One row per held document payment: document, hash, requester, approval, status
newRecordsNeeded.why: Holds the wait between 'asked in Frappe' and 'the chain confirmed'. A hook that throws rolls the row back, so the row lives in Core.

newRecordsNeeded.title: waiting for signature, paid, failed, hash mismatch, abandoned
newRecordsNeeded.why: The skeleton's request states. One state machine, one event, as the book's rules ask.

newRecordsNeeded.title: A held payment changed state
newRecordsNeeded.why: The funnel for 'pay an invoice from Frappe' reads it.

newRecordsNeeded.title: Prepare a payment for a Frappe document and return its approval
newRecordsNeeded.why: The skeleton's /prepare. Takes the document hash, cost centre and account code; refuses if the signer lacks the hat or the budget has no room.

newRecordsNeeded.title: The canonical form of a document that its hash covers
newRecordsNeeded.why: Skeleton CANON v1: sorted keys, fixed fields, 2-decimal amounts. Editing a draft after /prepare changes the hash, so the chain payment becomes an unmatched Bank Transaction.

newRecordsNeeded.title: A held payment posts only if the chain's document hash equals the draft's
newRecordsNeeded.why: This is the claim behind 'Frappe never marks money moved until the chain says so'.

newRecordsNeeded.title: The document changed after the payment was prepared
newRecordsNeeded.why: The skeleton's 'Mismatch' state needs a refusal code the CLI and door can print.

newRecordsNeeded.title: Cancelling or amending a paid document is a reversal transaction, never a deletion
newRecordsNeeded.why: START-HERE section 3. The skeleton refuses to cancel a posted Safe payment; a refund must be a chain event.

newRecordsNeeded.title: Every payment carries the document hash, the cost centre and the account code
newRecordsNeeded.why: START-HERE section 4. payments.prepare-command and the Payments contract probably change; the skeleton's contract is a stand-in.

newRecordsNeeded.title: Contract changes the skeleton forced
newRecordsNeeded.why: PaymentSent names no signer; a log names an org only by hash; a department is not authority; no canPay view; payment_failed leaves no log. Each is a contract change or a rule (FINDINGS, Core half).

newRecordsNeeded.title: The map from a hat to Frappe roles, limited to a department
newRecordsNeeded.why: A DocType on the site, so it can be read and changed there. The skeleton's default map failed real tasks (an admin could not create a Supplier).

newRecordsNeeded.title: One row per person, hat and department, with the roles it added
newRecordsNeeded.why: A role two hats give must stay while one remains; revoke removes only roles no remaining grant gives.

newRecordsNeeded.title: A hat granted or revoked on chain updates the person's Frappe roles
newRecordsNeeded.why: Measured: 0.1 to 0.4 s to apply. Core delivers the event; the app applies it.

newRecordsNeeded.title: Changing a person's roles by hand on the site is refused
newRecordsNeeded.why: Skeleton: a validate hook refuses it even for Administrator. It cannot stop the database or bench, so a nightly drift check is also needed.

newRecordsNeeded.title: Compare Frappe roles with the chain's hat grants and report any difference
newRecordsNeeded.why: The only backstop against a bypass (FINDINGS: raw SQL, bench console, ignore_validate).

newRecordsNeeded.title: The member hat creates an Employee, and the chain does not know gender or date of birth
newRecordsNeeded.why: ERPNext strips the Employee role from a User with no Employee. The skeleton used placeholders. The book must say where HR facts come from.

newRecordsNeeded.title: Show which Frappe roles each hat gives in this organisation
newRecordsNeeded.why: Programmatic and visible through the CLI, as Aaron asked for the feature switches.

newRecordsNeeded.title: The outbox: every chain event for a site, in order, with its delivery state
newRecordsNeeded.why: Replaces book-facts. Gap-free per organisation from 1; the key is chainId:txHash:logIndex (not blockHash, which a reorg changes).

newRecordsNeeded.title: Deliver events in order, resend from the number Frappe asks for, dedupe by key
newRecordsNeeded.why: At-least-once plus dedupe. Skeleton: 40 of 40 checks, including Frappe stopped when the log lands.

newRecordsNeeded.title: What happens when one event can never be applied
newRecordsNeeded.why: One failing event blocks every later event for that organisation, money included. Skeleton reproduced it. The design needs a dead-letter rule.

newRecordsNeeded.title: Which currency the books use when the Safe holds USDC
newRecordsNeeded.why: Skeleton books USDC 1:1 as USD. A GBP company needs a rate in the entry and in the hash. Not tried.

newRecordsNeeded.title: Chain events that arrive after a fiscal period closed post into the open period
newRecordsNeeded.why: START-HERE section 3.

newRecordsNeeded.title: Post the Payment Entry, matched to its document, with the transaction hash
newRecordsNeeded.why: Replaces books.record-money-fact. An unmatched hash becomes an unreconciled Bank Transaction.

newRecordsNeeded.title: One row per site: organisation, address, status, versions
newRecordsNeeded.why: Replaces org-heads, which holds an outside site's keys.

newRecordsNeeded.title: creating, ready, suspended, archived, failed
newRecordsNeeded.why: Re-creating a site for an organisation that already had events left the new site empty (FINDINGS). The states and the replay rule must be written.

newRecordsNeeded.title: A site changed state
newRecordsNeeded.why: Site creation is a journey step.

newRecordsNeeded.title: Create the site, then deliver the organisation's events from number 1
newRecordsNeeded.why: Skeleton: 143 s cold, 7 s again for the same slug. Safe to repeat.

newRecordsNeeded.title: Creates, upgrades and backs up sites; has a local fake for the devnet
newRecordsNeeded.why: Replaces frappe-head. Per-site backups and bench upgrades are a later need.

newRecordsNeeded.title: One bench serves many sites; AWS London; the app is a custom Frappe app on upstream, not a fork
newRecordsNeeded.why: START-HERE section 5. The skeleton needed no fork.

newRecordsNeeded.title: An organisation is one command and its site answers
newRecordsNeeded.why: Skeleton behaviour 1. First eval.

newRecordsNeeded.title: Grant a hat from inside Frappe and the roles follow
newRecordsNeeded.why: Skeleton behaviour 2.

newRecordsNeeded.title: Pay a Purchase Invoice from Frappe and see it land in the books
newRecordsNeeded.why: Skeleton behaviour 3.

newRecordsNeeded.title: A revert, a repeated event and Frappe down all end consistent
newRecordsNeeded.why: Skeleton behaviour 4.

newRecordsNeeded.title: One row per site and feature: on or off
newRecordsNeeded.why: Features the skeleton knows: accounts, people, payroll, projects, crm, whatsapp, stock, manufacturing.

newRecordsNeeded.title: off, installing, on
newRecordsNeeded.why: On installs what is missing; off never destroys data.

newRecordsNeeded.title: List an organisation's features
newRecordsNeeded.why: Replaces org head app list.

newRecordsNeeded.title: Turn a feature on (admin hat only)
newRecordsNeeded.why: Replaces org head app add. Core checks the hat on chain before it calls the site service.

newRecordsNeeded.title: Turn a feature off without losing data
newRecordsNeeded.why: Replaces org head app remove.

newRecordsNeeded.title: Turning a feature off destroys nothing, and turning it on shows everything again
newRecordsNeeded.why: Uninstalling an app is not 'off'.

newRecordsNeeded.why: Replaces the nine org head doc operations. All run as the calling person; Frappe decides. The money-document refusal goes (aaron.one-door).

newRecordsNeeded.title: List and describe a site's DocTypes (two operations)
newRecordsNeeded.why: Replaces org head doctype list and get.

newRecordsNeeded.why: The same decision pack. Replaces document render and export.

openForAaron.question: Does equity stay in the book? aaron.frappe-native keeps governance and equity. START-HERE and GROUNDING drop it.
options: drop: Archive the 38 operations, 7 tables, 7 machines, 27 decisions and 8 contracts (captable, options, rounds, exits, share-class, vesting, hats-elections, governor). Board and proposals stay.
park: Keep the records, mark them 'not built', and take them out of the first build layers. Reversible.
keep: Keep as written. The cap table and rounds are then a Core feature that Frappe does not have.
openForAaron.recommendation: park. GROUNDING says equity is not the direction and START-HERE says dropped, so build nothing now; but archiving 38 operations is hard to undo and costs nothing to defer. It is your ruling to rewrite either way.
openForAaron.affects: equity (38 operations, 27 decisions), org board handover, shareholder votes

openForAaron.question: Is the hosted FDE a product feature in the book, or an upsell that is sold and run outside it?
options: outside the book: Archive the 7 org.fde operations, 4 tables (and 1 devnet table), 3 machines, 2 procedures and 12 decisions. The FDE works through the CLI like any agent, wearing hats.
keep as agent: Keep one hosted agent per organisation that acts as its asker. Keep the hosting payment.
openForAaron.recommendation: outside the book. GROUNDING calls the FDE 'the upsell, not the base product', and START-HERE says it does not run day-to-day operations. An FDE is a person with agents; agents are already Core.
openForAaron.affects: 7 operations, 4 tables, 3 machines, 12 decisions including aaron.fde-agent, fde-anyone, fde-hosted, test-prices

openForAaron.question: Do on-chain pay agreements (offer, accept, collect) stay now that payroll is Frappe's?
options: keep in payments: Move the 11 operations and 2 tables to payments. A contractor or stream can be paid on chain with no payroll.
drop: Payroll runs are the only salary path, paid through payment.send.
openForAaron.recommendation: keep in payments. They are money and authority on chain, which is Core by your own rule. They are not payroll calculation.
openForAaron.affects: 11 operations, tables agreements and agreement-writes, contract agreements

openForAaron.question: Do hats stay as they are, with one budget per organisation, or do budgets become department-scoped?
options: hats as-is, budget change: Roles follow the four hats. The Budgets contract enforces a budget per department. This is the contract change START-HERE 4 expects.
hats as-is, one budget: Department is only a label on the event. A department limit on Frappe is cosmetic.
custom: Design something new. The spike gives no reason to.
openForAaron.recommendation: hats as-is, budget change. The skeleton's four hats did the work; its only real gap is that a department is not authority on the stand-in contracts.
openForAaron.affects: budgets, payments.document-fields, the Budgets contract, hat-role-map

openForAaron.question: How does a UK company file payroll with HMRC?
options: provider API: An integration record, no payroll engine of our own.
bureau: A partner files; we only export.
build RTI: A large build on top of Frappe HR.
openForAaron.recommendation: provider API. It closes the gap without building it, and a later swap is one integration record.
openForAaron.affects: one new integration; payroll stays reached either way

openForAaron.question: Is Capxul still sold to individuals (a personal address book, a payment inbox, referrals, a waitlist), or only to companies?
options: companies only now: Keep the personal Safe (every signer needs one). Park referral, waitlist, personal contacts and the personal inbox as later.
both: Keep as written. A person without a company has no Frappe site, so their address book stays in Core.
openForAaron.recommendation: companies only now. GROUNDING sells to 15 to 25 person companies. These verdicts are marked low confidence until you answer.
openForAaron.affects: referral, waitlist, contact, inbox, request (about 20 operations)
